question: Using Signac and Seurat, jointly analyze a single-cell multi-omic dataset measuring chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) and gene expression (scRNA-seq) in the same cells; then generate a UMAP based solely on the chromatin accessibility data and a joint UMAP integrating both modalities.

files.eval_guideline: Plot must show two UMAP panels -- one for ATAC-only clusters and one for joint RNA+ATAC clusters -- with cells colored by cluster assignment; panel arrangement, color scheme, and point styling may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The files have the identical basename and PNG image format. The name and task context indicate both contain the requested chromatin-only and joint multi-modal UMAP visualizations.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic plot content: two UMAP panels representing ATAC-only and joint RNA+ATAC clustering, with cells colored by cluster. Exact pixels, layout, colors, and point styling may differ, so semantic comparison is appropriate.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images satisfy the core visualization requirement: each contains two side-by-side UMAP panels, with an ATAC-only embedding on the left and a joint RNA+ATAC embedding on the right. Cells are colored by cluster assignment, clusters are numerically labeled, and both panels have appropriate UMAP axes and informative titles. Thus, they communicate the same broad scientific comparison between chromatin-only and multimodal clustering. However, the underlying results are visibly different. The reference displays clusters numbered approximately 0–21, whereas the candidate displays only 0–16. Cluster geometry, relative positions, connectivity, sizes, and isolated populations differ substantially in both panels; for example, the reference joint embedding has a large lower cluster centered near UMAP2 -7 and several right-side islands, while the candidate has differently arranged upper-right and lower-left structures. These differences exceed cosmetic variation and suggest different preprocessing, parameters, clustering resolution, or data subsets. The candidate is therefore structurally compliant and scientifically analogous, but it does not reproduce the same data patterns closely enough to be fully equivalent.
